title: VisitDoc golden-set case
description: One labelled patient message. The label attaches to a request, not to a message: `requests` is the expected segmentation, in order. Anything derivable from `requests` is deliberately absent - see README.md.

family.description: What this case is here to exercise. Grouping only - not scored.

message.description: The patient's message, verbatim, as one turn.

history.description: Prior turns, oldest first. Present only where the label depends on them.

requests.description: The expected segmentation. Array order IS the expected order; position is not stored separately.

gist.description: A human reference for what this request asks. NOT SCORED - a segment has many valid restatements, and exact-matching the classifier's wording would measure phrasing, not segmentation.

answerable.description: faq_question only. true when the pinned corpus answers this request, false when it is a gap. Two-valued on purpose: FaqVerdict's four abstentions are identical in behaviour and nothing may branch on which one it is, so only `FaqVerdict.answered` is labelable by hand.

cites.description: faq_question only. Corpus entry ids from corpus.json the answer must rest on. Non-empty exactly when answerable is true.

tools.description: booking only. The tools whose absence means the request was not served - a required subset, not a sequence. A check_availability that precedes a book_appointment is not a miss.

source.description: Where the case came from: `<spec>/<set>#<id>`, or `new`. A `(relabelled)` or `(re-expressed)` suffix means PROVENANCE.md records what changed.

note.description: Why the case is here, or what is fragile about its label.
